why: The quote is verbatim (prompt-caching.md:204, whole line: 'Set `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` to force the five-minute TTL regardless of authentication. This is useful when you're debugging cache behavior, comparing the two TTLs, or overriding an `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` set in managed settings.'). The identifier half of the finding also holds: a NUL-safe `grep -ra 'FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M|ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H' packages apps scripts` returns zero hits. But BOTH stated consequences are false, which is the classic 'identifier unwired, consequence already handled one layer up' shape. (1) 'No local override of a policy-delivered value' is wrong: `extendedPromptCache: false` is not a passive default, it is an ACTIVE force-5m. `upgradePromptCacheTtl` (unified-network-interceptor.ts:437) opens with `if (!isExtendedPromptCacheEnabled()) return stripPromptCacheTtl(body)`, and `stripPromptCacheTtl` (:367-414) deletes `ttl` from every ephemeral `cache_control` block in tools, system, message content and top-level. Its own comment names the exact scenario the doc names: 'When extendedPromptCache is disabled, the SDK may still send ttl: "1h" natively (via prompt-caching-scope beta). This function removes the ttl field so blocks fall back to the API default (5 min).' It is called unconditionally from the Anthropic provider's `modifyRequest` (:978), i.e. on the wire, DOWNSTREAM of the SDK -- so it overrides whatever the SDK chose from authentication or from an inherited env var, which is strictly more authoritative than `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M`, and it is the default. The doc's stated purpose (overriding a managed-settings `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`) is therefore already satisfied: an unclassified key in a managed `env` block lands in `process.env` as category `immediate` (config/managed-env.ts) and is inherited by the SDK subprocess, and our strip removes the resulting 1h TTL anyway. `extendedPromptCache` itself is a per-user config.json key that no managed-policy path writes, so there is nothing policy-delivered to be trapped by. (2) 'Reachable only through the desktop Settings -> AI toggle and its RPC pair ... no way to set the TTL on the headless server or in CI' is wrong twice over. It is a documented user-editable config.json key -- docs-site/content/reference/config/config-file.md:169 and the ru mirror :172 -- living at `CONFIG_DIR/config.json`, where `CONFIG_DIR` honours `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` (config/paths.ts:19-21). The consumer that applies the TTL is the interceptor inside the SDK subprocess, which reads that file straight off disk with a 100 ms cache (interceptor-common.ts:104-114) and never touches the renderer or the RPC layer; the repo's own suite drives both branches by writing the key into config.json (unified-network-interceptor.schema.test.ts:156,163), which is the CI recipe the finding says does not exist. And the RPC pair is registered in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/settings.ts:401,407 -- the HEADLESS server's own handler table, allow-listed for remote at protocol/routing.ts:166-167; apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts:358-359 is a client of it, not its owner. So the RPC pair is a headless-server surface, not a desktop-only one. Context that makes this naming rather than behaviour: this fork replaces CLAUDE_*/ANTHROPIC_* env knobs with config.json keys under `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` repo-wide, and the same sweep already reached that conclusion for this exact knob on another page -- 2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3361: '`1h` prompt-cache TTL exists under our own `extendedPromptCache` config key rather than `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` ... env-var naming, not a behaviour gap.' f197 contradicts it. Also relevant, though not §3 of the inert worklist (this is not one of the nine): docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-prompt-cache-and-egress-disclosure.md:121, harvested into the deviation register, records that the knob only rewrites `cache_control`, which only the Anthropic adapter emits, while the shipped Pi/Nestor path is an OpenAI-like relay with implicit prefix caching and no cache writes -- and `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default -- so an env override would have nothing to act on for the shipped product. Cited line numbers had drifted (storage.ts:129/173/1030 are now :134/:178/:1035; interceptor-common.ts:143 is now :141-145); content matched, so that alone is not the refutation.
correctedState: Both documented TTL controls exist in this fork under one config.json boolean rather than two env vars: `extendedPromptCache: true` == `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1`, and `extendedPromptCache: false` (the default) == `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1`. The 5m force is not passive -- `upgradePromptCacheTtl` delegates to `stripPromptCacheTtl` (unified-network-interceptor.ts:367-437), which deletes `ttl` from every ephemeral cache_control block in tools, system, messages and top-level on every outbound Anthropic request (:978), explicitly to undo a 1h TTL the SDK injected on its own. Because it runs on the wire after the SDK, it overrides auth-based auto-selection and any `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` inherited from a managed `env` block -- the doc's stated use case, satisfied by default. The knob is settable outside the desktop UI: it is a documented config.json key (docs-site .../config-file.md:169) under `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR`-aware `CONFIG_DIR`, read directly by the SDK subprocess's interceptor, and its RPC getter/setter is registered on the headless server (server-core/.../rpc/settings.ts:401,407) and remote-allow-listed (protocol/routing.ts:166-167). What genuinely differs is spelling, plus the absence of auto-selection by auth type -- and that half is already registered against docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-prompt-cache-and-egress-disclosure.md:121, whose reason (cache_control is emitted only by the Anthropic adapter, which is flag-off; the shipped Pi/Nestor relay does implicit prefix caching with no cache writes) applies to the override variables too.
